definitions: To draw liquid from (a container or source).
To make use of a resource.
To fit a tap or a spile to (a cask) in order to draw off the liquid.
To obtain information or a signal from a telephone or other line by means of a secret listening device.
examples: She tapped him on the shoulder.
They tapped the maple tree for syrup.
We need to tap into new markets.
The plumber tapped the new barrel.
Their phone calls were being tapped.
